title: Reinforcing L2 reading comprehension through artificial intelligence intervention: refining engagement to foster self-regulated learning
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether an artificial intelligence (AI) intervention can improve second-language (L2) reading comprehension while also increasing learner engagement and self-regulated learning. The study addresses a gap in the literature on AI-supported reading instruction, especially for language learners, by asking whether AI-enhanced classrooms produce better reading, engagement, and self-regulation outcomes than more conventional instruction, and how learners perceive such environments.

The intervention centered on the ReadToMe (RTM) platform, an AI-based reading support system that converted course content into a multisensory format. RTM included text-to-speech, synchronized word highlighting, pronunciation support, images, word translation, dictionary functions, knowledge-graph features, recording and analysis of student reading, and automated feedback/remediation. The experimental group used RTM for homework and reading support, while the control group received traditional reading instruction and feedback from the instructor or classmates. The study used a mixed-methods design with pre/post quantitative measures and follow-up semi-structured interviews.

Participants were 60 Iranian female EFL students drawn from two intact classes at a language institute, with 30 students in the experimental group and 30 in the control group. They were upper-intermediate English learners (around C1 level), mean age 21, attending in-person sessions twice weekly for approximately 12 weeks. Both groups used the same reading textbook, and the same instructor taught both groups. Quantitative instruments measured reading comprehension, engagement, and self-regulation; qualitative interviews explored students’ experiences with the instructional approaches.

The main findings were that the AI-supported group significantly outperformed the control group in reading comprehension, self-regulation, and engagement. Interview data reinforced these results: many students described the AI platform as motivating, engaging, and useful for personalized feedback and comprehension support. At the same time, some students reported usability problems such as slow loading and navigation difficulties. Overall, the paper concludes that AI-enhanced reading environments can effectively support L2 reading development and related learner processes, though technical design and usability remain important considerations.

identified_tools.name: ReadToMe
identified_tools.description: An AI-based reading and comprehension platform (RTM) that converts curriculum text into a multi-sensory learning format with text-to-speech, pronunciation localization, concept images, knowledge graphs, recording/analysis, automated assessment, and remediation features.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the experimental intervention in an upper-intermediate Iranian EFL reading course over 12 weeks to support L2 reading comprehension, engagement, and self-regulated learning through AI-assisted homework and class-aligned reading activities.

findings.finding_summary: In a mixed-methods controlled study, the experimental group using ReadToMe outperformed the control group on post-instruction reading comprehension after controlling for pretest scores. ANCOVA showed a significant group effect, F(1, 59)=43.82, p=0.000, partial η2=0.167; descriptive results showed the experimental group increased from M=11.58 (SD=0.93) pre-intervention to M=28.21 (SD=0.99) post-intervention, versus the control group from M=11.62 (SD=0.72) to M=13.11 (SD=0.89).
findings.measure: Reading comprehension test developed by Tong et al. (2017): two reading passages, 24 multiple-choice questions, and 6 open-ended questions; maximum score 30

findings.finding_summary: ReadToMe produced a significant positive effect on self-regulated learning relative to the control condition. ANCOVA reported F(1, 59)=19.23, p=0.011, partial η2=0.151; descriptively, the experimental group improved from M=2.23 (SD=0.85) to M=4.78 (SD=0.98), compared with the control group from M=2.31 (SD=0.92) to M=2.67 (SD=0.69).

The AI intervention significantly improved learner engagement compared with traditional instruction. ANCOVA found a significant group effect, F(1, 59)=24.11, p=0.000, partial η2=0.171; descriptively, the experimental group rose from M=2.11 (SD=1.15) to M=4.67 (SD=0.99), while the control group changed from M=2.15 (SD=0.95) to M=2.17 (SD=0.89).
findings.measure: Revised School Engagement Scale measuring behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement

findings.finding_summary: Qualitative interview findings indicated generally positive student perceptions of ReadToMe, with 77% of students highlighting the AI platform’s effectiveness in fostering engagement and supporting self-regulation, including themes such as increased attentiveness and enhanced motivation. However, 23% identified usability barriers, especially system responsiveness and interface design issues, and example comments referenced slow loading times and difficulty navigating the platform.
findings.measure: Semi-structured interviews on student perceptions of the AI-enhanced classroom

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods pilot with experimental and control groups and pre/post measures, but it uses intact classes, a small sample (n=60), and does not present a full randomized controlled trial design. That places it below strong causal evidence tiers.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported partial eta-squared values for reading comprehension (0.167), self-regulation (0.151), and engagement (0.171) indicate statistically significant but modest effects by the provided framework thresholds (<0.20). Results are consistently positive, though impact magnitude does not reach the blue tier cutoff.
